R-SUG-10.template: R-SUG-10 · {column} names the customer: {customers} distinct customers over {rows} rows

R-SUG-11.template: R-SUG-11 · {column} names the order: {orders} orders over {rows} rows

R-SUG-12.template: R-SUG-12 · {flow} ÷ distinct {order}: the average value of an order ({orders} orders)

R-SUG-13.template: R-SUG-13 · {quantity} ÷ distinct {order}: how many units an order holds

R-SUG-14.template: R-SUG-14 · Σ {flow} ÷ Σ {quantity}: the average price paid per unit, weighted by the units (a ratio of sums, not a mean of prices)

R-SUG-15.template: R-SUG-15 · {flow} ÷ distinct {customer}: what one customer brings ({customers} customers)

R-SUG-16.weight.template: weight {weight} for this kind of KPI

R-SUG-17.event.template: the date of the event itself, preferred to {dates}

R-SUG-17.none.template: R-SUG-17 · No time axis: {never} is a birth date

R-SUG-19.template: R-SUG-19 · Split by {column}: amounts in {count} currencies are never added together

R-SUG-20.template: R-SUG-20 · {revenue} and the cost {cost}: the margin (Σ {revenue} - Σ {cost}) ÷ Σ {revenue}, in percent

R-SUG-21.template: R-SUG-21 · {profit} is what is left of {revenue}: Σ {profit} ÷ Σ {revenue} is the margin, in percent

R-SUG-22.template: R-SUG-22 · {column} is a status ({tracked} against {opposite}): the share of rows that are {states}

R-SUG-22.key.template: R-SUG-22 · {column} is a status ({tracked} against {opposite}): the share of distinct {key} that are {states}

R-SUG-23.template: R-SUG-23 · Weighted by {weight}: Σ({column} x {weight}) ÷ Σ {weight}, so a value on 100 units counts 100 times (rows without a positive {weight} are left out)

R-SUG-24.template: R-SUG-24 · {start} then {end}: the average number of days between the two

R-SUG-28.template: R-SUG-28 · {column} is a measure without a role (no amount, quantity or price): averaged, as its sum rarely means anything

R-SUG-28.surface.template: R-SUG-28 · {column} is a surface: averaged, as its sum rarely means anything

R-TIME-02.template: The dates come about once a {typical}: shown by {typical} instead of by {requested} (R-TIME-02).

R-TIME-03.template: By {requested} would draw over {periods} periods: shown by {coarser} instead (R-TIME-03).

R-TIME-04.template: R-TIME-04 · {total} left out of the time axis:

R-TIME-04.end.template: . Clean can read the placeholders as missing.

R-TIME-04.part_placeholder.template: {rows} dated {day} (a placeholder meaning {meaning}, not a real date)

R-TIME-04.undated.template: {count} rows without a date are left out.

R-TIME-04.undated#one.template: {count} row without a date is left out.

R-TYP-01.template: {share} of values, such as {examples}, cannot be read as numbers: kept as text so that no value is lost (R-TYP-01)

R-TYP-02.template: words in place of numbers ({words}: {share} of values) read as missing (R-TYP-02)

R-TYP-03.template: {share} of values start with 0 (e.g. {examples}): a code, kept as text so the zeros stay (R-TYP-03)

R-TYP-04.category.template: the name says a category ('{word}'): whole numbers read as category codes, not as a measure (R-TYP-04)

R-TYP-04.code.template: the name says a code or a number ('{word}'): whole numbers read as codes, not as a measure (R-TYP-04)

R-TYP-04.sign.template: the name says a code or a number (a number sign): whole numbers read as codes, not as a measure (R-TYP-04)

R-TYP-05.length.template: {share} of values have exactly {digits} digits: a code (a measure would vary in length) (R-TYP-05)

R-TYP-05.unique.template: all values are different whole numbers of {digits} digits: an identifier, not a measure (R-TYP-05)

R-TYP-06.template: {share} of values read as dates in two formats ({first} and {second}) (R-TYP-06)

R-TYP-07.template: {share} of values are times of day ({format}, e.g. {examples}): read as hours since midnight (R-TYP-07)

R-TYP-07.stored.template: stored as a time of day: read as hours since midnight (07:40 → 7.67) (R-TYP-07)

R-TYP-09.template: {share} of values are lists separated by ';' of {count} choices (e.g. {examples}): a multiple-choice answer, not categories (R-TYP-09)

R-TYP-10.template: values are ranges ordered by their lower bound: {order} (R-TYP-10)

R-TYP-11.template: the name says a count: 0 and 1 kept as numbers (R-TYP-11)

R-TYP-12.template: {columns} look like the parts of one date: Clean proposes to assemble them into a '{name}' column (B-20) (R-TYP-12)

R-TYP-13.template: '{note}' closing the name is a note, not the word it is about (R-TYP-13)

R-TYP-14.template: the name says 'total' with no money word and the values are whole numbers: read as a count, not an amount (R-TYP-14)

R-TYP-15.ambiguous.template: '{either}' reads both as a decimal and as thousands, and no value tells: the dot is read as the decimal point, the comma as a thousands separator (ambiguous) (R-TYP-15)

R-TYP-15.comma.template: comma read as the decimal separator: {only} values such as '{value}' read only this way ({both} such as '{either}' read both ways) (R-TYP-15)

R-TYP-15.decimal_comma.template: the comma is read as the decimal separator: '{either}' could be thousands, but numbers up to {largest} are written without one (R-TYP-15)

R-TYP-15.decimal_dot.template: the dot is read as the decimal separator: '{either}' could be thousands, but numbers up to {largest} are written without one (R-TYP-15)

R-TYP-15.dot.template: dot read as the decimal point: {only} values such as '{value}' read only this way ({both} such as '{either}' read both ways) (R-TYP-15)

R-TYP-15.thousands_comma.template: the comma is read as a thousands separator: the {both} values with one have groups of three digits (such as '{either}') and the {plain} numbers written without one are all below 1,000 (R-TYP-15)

R-TYP-15.thousands_dot.template: the dot is read as a thousands separator: the {both} values with one have groups of three digits (such as '{either}') and the {plain} numbers written without one are all below 1,000 (R-TYP-15)

TYP.addresses.template: {share} look like street addresses (a number and a street word)

TYP.day_first.template: day/month order is ambiguous: day first assumed

TYP.discrete.template: only {count} distinct whole numbers: shown as categories

TYP.kept_text.template: kept as text to preserve leading zeros and formatting

TYP.labels.template: few stop words ({stopwords}) and little sentence punctuation ({punctuation}): short labels

TYP.name_labels.template: name suggests {role}, but values are short labels

TYP.row_index.template: row numbers left by an export (pandas index)

TYP.shared_key.template: only {share} unique values: a reference shared by rows, used as categories

TYP.top20.template: the 20 most frequent values cover {share} of rows
